findings.title: Negative offset queryset slicing will raise an exception, not provide pagination
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly disallows negative indices in slices and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` (it does not fall back to Python list-style negative indexing). Any authorized caller (superuser or org member with global access) that supplies a cursor with a negative offset (e.g. by crafting `cursor=0:-1:0`) while passing `optimized_pagination=true` will cause the endpoint to raise an unhandled exception and return a 500, rather than the 'efficient reverse pagination' described in the comments. The advertised 'advanced feature' is non-functional and introduces a crash vector that is trivially triggerable by any user who qualifies for `enable_advanced` access.

findings.title: Misleading comments claim negative-offset pagination is handled safely by the ORM
findings.body: The comments above the negative-offset branch state 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' and 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level.' Both claims are incorrect: Django raises an exception on negative slice bounds (see the related bug finding), and the comment about permissions is irrelevant to the actual failure mode. These comments will mislead future maintainers into believing the negative-offset code path is tested/working when it is not.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError if organization_context.member is None
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise `AttributeError` if `organization_context.member` is `None` and `request.user.is_superuser` is False (e.g. a non-superuser context where member lookup failed/is absent). There is no null-check before accessing `.has_global_access`, so a legitimate request from a user without `is_superuser` but with a falsy/missing `member` will crash the endpoint instead of falling back to the standard DateTimePaginator path.

findings.title: Comment describes a change that was not made
findings.body: The added comment claims 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios' but the line below (`self.offset = int(offset)`) is unchanged from before this PR and already allowed negative integers. The comment implies new functionality was added here when nothing functionally changed, which is confusing and inaccurate documentation that could mislead future readers into thinking this file enables/validates the new negative-offset feature.

findings.title: No tests added for new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: This PR adds a new ~100-line paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator) with a distinct code path (including the broken negative-offset handling) and new branching logic in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get (optimized_pagination query param, enable_advanced permission check), but no test files were added or modified. Given the duplicated/complex logic and the permission-gated behavior, the lack of tests means the negative-offset crash bug (and the permission-gating logic in the endpoint) would not be caught by CI.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result with no real optimization
findings.body: Aside from the broken negative-offset branch, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-exact copy of BasePaginator.get_result (same query building, extra/offset handling, cursor building). This duplicates logic that will now need to be kept in sync in two places, while providing no actual performance benefit described in the PR title ('Enhanced Pagination Performance') — the only behavioral delta is the non-functional negative offset path. This increases maintenance risk without delivering the claimed performance improvement.
